free_tier.stated: Vendor help page states it outright: 'Unlimited storage and distribution for mods and images that you create. Unlimited file hosting for mods and images that you've created and uploaded.' Their own wiki table: Maximum Storage 'Unrestricted', Upload Limitations 'Unlimited (20GB limit through the browser, contact us for larger uploads)'.

egress.terms: Free, no egress quota. But per-IP shaped (see reliability_note). No Cloudflare in front of the file CDN; downloads come from their own edge.

interface_detail: Web upload + REST API v1 (api.nexusmods.com, `users/validate.json` returned 401 unauthenticated = live and auth-gated, not dead). Free API key issued per account.
tooling: REST + a maintained community uploader (Digitalroot.ModUploader, supports `nexusmods` commands).
chaining: Offers 20 GB per object with no aggregate storage quota. Downloads require session authentication or API keys, operating as an archive store rather than a direct origin.
limits_note: per-object-cap 20 GB via browser, larger by request. per-ip-shaping is the binding number: ~1 MB/s regular, ~1.5 MB/s with an adblocker, 3 MB/s Supporters; uncapped only for Premium (paid). Resumable downloads are free only on files >500 MB.
reliability_note: The 1–1.5 MB/s un-premium cap is the real constraint. ~3.5–5 GB/hour per stream, so per-IP-shaping governs, not storage. Files are virus-scanned and quarantined on false positives (WinRAR .rar especially).

extras.agent_focus: Print-on-demand, media and fulfilment platforms that host your uploads permanently and serve them cheaply. The question for every candidate was NOT 'can I upload' (all of them accept uploads) but: does the platform serve my ORIGINAL bytes back, unsigned, indefinitely, from a CDN I can hot-link? POD image hosts (Redbubble/Printful/Printify/Society6/Threadless/Zazzle/Etsy) all re-encode, cap at 20-300 MB and gate the write behind account setup — they are inverted (tiny ingress, no egress). The value in this niche is the DIGITAL-PRODUCT fulfilment layer and the 3D-model repositories, which are the two places where arbitrary file types survive ingest at GB scale.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
